text.p: Pilots, co-pilots and engineers at Yemen Airways held a one-day strike on Thursday to demand better pay, disrupting air traffic to and from the Arab state, an airline official said.
The 160 strikers threatened to hold more protests starting Tuesday if the airline's board of directors failed to heed their demands by midnight Thursday (2100 GMT), he told Reuters.
"Work today went on normally from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., but after that no Yemen Airways flights took off or landed, whether on an internal or on a foreign trip," he said.
"They said they would repeat the same protest on Tuesday if the issue is not solved and might escalate it after that until their demands are met."
He gave no further details and did not say what salary increases they were pressing for. The strikers were not available for comment.
The strike did not affect flights by other airlines servicing Yemen, the official said.

Yemen Airways pays its pilots and co-pilots between 35,000 rials ($280) and 75,000 rials a month, depending on the duration of service with the company. This has forced some of the flight staff to join other regional carriers who offer better salaries.
The Sanaa-based airline was formed last year by the merger of Yemenia Airways and al-Yemda -- the carriers of the former North Yemen and South Yemen which united in 1990.
With a fleet of 13 aircraft -- four Boeing 727s, one Boeing 707, three Boeing 737s, three de Havilland Dash-7s and two Airbus A310s -- the airline flies to 23 destinations in Asia, Africa and Europe.
